description: Evaluation cases for the mops-cli skill. Tests whether agents produce correct mops.toml configuration, use canister names (not file paths) with mops check, pin toolchain versions, use mo:core (not mo:base), handle migration workflows correctly, and avoid documented pitfalls.

output_evals.name: New project setup
output_evals.prompt: I want to start a new Motoko project. Walk me through setting up mops from scratch, including the mops.toml and the initial commands. Just the setup, no deployment steps.
expected_behaviors: Runs `mops init -y` to initialize the project
Uses `mops toolchain use moc latest` (or a specific version) — NOT the bare `mops toolchain use moc` which opens an interactive picker
Includes `[toolchain]` section in mops.toml with a concrete `moc` version
Includes `[dependencies]` with `core` (not `base`)
Includes `[canisters.<name>]` with a `main` field pointing to the entry file
Runs `mops add core` to install the core library
Does NOT suggest installing mo:base

output_evals.name: Adding a dependency
output_evals.prompt: How do I add the `serde` package at version 1.3.0 as a regular dependency to my mops project?
expected_behaviors: Uses `mops add serde@1.3.0`
Explains that this updates both mops.toml and mops.lock
Does NOT suggest manually editing mops.toml to add the dependency

output_evals.name: Running mops check
output_evals.prompt: I have a canister called `backend` defined in mops.toml. How do I type-check it and auto-fix any lint issues?
expected_behaviors: Uses `mops check backend` (canister name, NOT a file path like src/backend/main.mo)
Mentions `mops check --fix` for auto-fixing
Does NOT pass a file path like `mops check src/backend/main.mo`

output_evals.name: Pinning moc version
output_evals.prompt: How do I pin the moc compiler to version 1.5.1 in my mops project?
expected_behaviors: Uses `mops toolchain use moc 1.5.1` OR shows manually editing `[toolchain]` in mops.toml
Shows the resulting `[toolchain]` section in mops.toml with `moc = "1.5.1"`
Does NOT use `mops toolchain use moc` without a version (that opens an interactive picker)

output_evals.name: Updating moc to latest
output_evals.prompt: I want to update moc to the latest version. What's the correct command?
expected_behaviors: If moc is already in [toolchain]: uses `mops toolchain update moc`
Alternatively mentions `mops toolchain use moc latest` as an option
Does NOT use `mops toolchain use moc` without a version
Clarifies that `toolchain update` only works when moc already has a [toolchain] entry

output_evals.name: Migration workflow
output_evals.prompt: My mops check is failing with a migration compatibility hint. How do I add a new migration called `AddEmailField` for my `backend` canister that uses enhanced migration?
expected_behaviors: Recommends `mops check --fix` (or `mops check backend`) to verify the migration resolves the error
Places `mops build` after the check step — never before
Does NOT suggest `mops migrate new` (command no longer exists)
Does NOT suggest `mops migrate freeze` (command no longer exists)
Does NOT suggest adding `--enhanced-migration` to mops.toml manually (mops auto-injects it)

output_evals.name: Warning flag configuration
output_evals.prompt: How do I enable M0236 (dot notation), M0237 (redundant explicit arguments), and M0223 (redundant type instantiation) as warnings for all canisters in my project?
expected_behaviors: Adds `-W=M0223,M0236,M0237` to the `args` list under `[moc]` in mops.toml
Places this in `[moc]` (global), not in `[canisters.<name>]`
Explains that -W= enables these optional checks as warnings
Does NOT place warning flags in [build].args (those are build-only)

output_evals.name: Replica tests pocket-ic pin
output_evals.prompt: I'm adding replica-mode tests (actor files / `// @testmode replica`) to my mops project and `mops test` errors saying pocket-ic isn't pinned. Briefly explain why it errors (not just a warning) and give me the config fix.
expected_behaviors: Pins `pocket-ic` in the `[toolchain]` section of mops.toml, or via `mops toolchain use pocket-ic <version>`, using a version `9.0.0` or higher (e.g. `15.0.0`) — not a version below `9.0.0`
Does NOT invent a `mops toolchain init` command (no such command exists in mops)
Does NOT claim this is only a warning that can be ignored
Does NOT suggest a dfx replica fallback still exists

output_evals.name: Adversarial: mops publish --dry-run scope
output_evals.prompt: Before publishing my package to the mops registry, I ran `mops publish --dry-run` and it passed. Does that mean the real `mops publish` is guaranteed to succeed? Just answer the question.
expected_behaviors: Explains that `--dry-run` runs the same local publish pipeline (packaging checks, docs, changelog, tests, benchmarks) but stops before identity/upload (no registry contact)
Clarifies it does NOT validate canister config (SPDX/semver/name rules)
Clarifies it does NOT prove registry acceptance (already published, permissions, missing deps)
Does NOT claim a passing `--dry-run` guarantees the real publish will succeed

output_evals.name: check-stable baseline bootstrap
output_evals.prompt: I'm starting a brand-new mops project and want to enable `check-stable`. There's no deployed version yet, so what do I use as the `.most` baseline for `[check-stable].path`? Just the setup, no deploy steps.
expected_behaviors: Uses `mops deployed init <canister>` to bootstrap the empty-actor baseline
Explains `mops deployed init` also sets `[check-stable].path` in mops.toml
Does NOT tell the user to hand-write a trivial `.most` file (e.g. `// Version: 1.0.0\nactor { };`)
May note the default destination is `deployed/<name>.most`

output_evals.name: Post-deploy .most promotion
output_evals.prompt: After I deploy my `backend` canister, how do I keep the `check-stable` baseline in sync with what's actually deployed? Just the command and where it should run.
expected_behaviors: Uses `mops deployed backend` (or `mops deployed` for all canisters) after a successful deploy
Explains it promotes the built `.most` (from `[build].outputDir`, default `.mops/.build`) to `deployed/<name>.most`
Notes it should run in the deploy pipeline immediately after deploy
Does NOT claim `mops deployed` regenerates or rebuilds the `.most` (it errors if the source is missing)

output_evals.name: Regenerating candid interface
output_evals.prompt: I changed the public interface of my `backend` Motoko canister and want to regenerate its `.did` file. What's the mops command and what does it do? No deploy steps.
expected_behaviors: Uses `mops generate candid backend` (or `mops generate candid` for all canisters)
Explains it (re)generates the `.did` from the current Motoko source
May note the result is committed alongside `mops.toml`
Does NOT suggest hand-editing the `.did` file or using `dfx generate`

output_evals.name: Autofix trimmed migrations with --no-check-limit
output_evals.prompt: My canister has `check-limit` set on its migration chain, but I need to run `mops check --fix` across the older, normally-trimmed migrations too. How?
expected_behaviors: Adds `--no-check-limit` to the command (e.g. `mops check --fix --no-check-limit`)
Explains `--no-check-limit` overrides `check-limit` for a single run
Does NOT suggest permanently removing or raising `check-limit` in mops.toml as the only option

output_evals.name: Adversarial: file path to mops check
output_evals.prompt: I want to type-check my canister. My main file is at src/backend/main.mo. I'll run: mops check src/backend/main.mo. Is that right?
expected_behaviors: Corrects the approach — for canister projects, always use the canister name, not a file path
Provides the correct command: `mops check backend` (using the canister name from mops.toml)
Explains that using a file path bypasses per-canister args in mops.toml
Does NOT endorse `mops check src/backend/main.mo` as correct for canister projects

output_evals.name: Adversarial: mo:base import
output_evals.prompt: I need a HashMap in my Motoko canister. Can I use `import HashMap "mo:base/HashMap"`?
expected_behaviors: Explains that mo:base is deprecated and should not be used
Redirects to mo:core as the replacement
Does NOT confirm that mo:base/HashMap is a valid choice

output_evals.name: Enabling Wasm optimization
output_evals.prompt: How do I turn on wasm-opt optimization for my mops build? Just the mops.toml config and any toolchain command, no deploy steps.
expected_behaviors: Adds an `[optimize]` section to mops.toml (default level `O3`)
Pins Binaryen via `mops toolchain use wasm-opt 131` (or `latest`) — states this pin is required; mops no longer auto-pins it
Notes a `wasm-opt` failure now fails the build (no longer soft-fails to an unoptimized Wasm)
Explains the optimization pass runs during `mops build`, and that `--no-optimize` skips it for a single run
Does NOT tell the user to invoke the `wasm-opt` binary manually or configure optimization through dfx

output_evals.name: mops install --locked (v3 lockfile flag)
output_evals.prompt: My old mops workflow used `mops install --lock check` in CI. What's the mops v3 equivalent, and does the CI env var still matter? Just answer directly.
expected_behaviors: Explains the `--lock` flag was removed in v3, replaced by `--locked`
Uses `mops install --locked` (fails if the lock is missing or would change; never writes it)
Explains the `CI` env var no longer affects lockfile behavior in v3 (previously it defaulted to `--lock check`)
Does NOT suggest `mops install --lock check` or `mops install --lock update` (removed flags)

output_evals.name: mops verify command
output_evals.prompt: I suspect a file inside `.mops/` was hand-edited after install. How do I check for that with mops? Just the command and what it checks.
expected_behaviors: Uses `mops verify`
Explains it re-hashes `.mops/` against `mops.lock`, and `mops.lock` against the registry
Notes it covers GitHub dependencies as well as registry ones
Does NOT claim `mops install` alone catches this — `mops install` no longer re-hashes `.mops/` on every run in v3

output_evals.name: mops build --check-deploy
output_evals.prompt: I want to catch canister installation failures (bad init args, module validation) before actually deploying. Is there a mops build flag for that? Just the flag and what it validates.
expected_behaviors: Uses `mops build --check-deploy` (or `[build].check-deploy = true` in mops.toml)
Explains it installs each built Wasm on a fresh PocketIC canister to catch module validation, initialization, and installation failures
Notes it requires `[toolchain] pocket-ic` pinned (`9.0.0`+) or `MOPS_POCKET_IC_URL` set to a running server
Does NOT claim this replaces an actual deploy — it's a pre-deploy validation step

output_evals.name: Running benchmarks
output_evals.prompt: I have benchmark files under bench/ in my mops project. How do I run them, save a baseline, and compare a later run against it? Just the commands.
expected_behaviors: Uses `mops bench` to run benchmarks in `bench/*.bench.mo`
Uses `mops bench --save` to save results as a baseline
Uses `mops bench --compare` to compare against saved results
Does NOT invent a non-existent command or suggest a manual benchmarking harness
